description: Erection of a single storey side extension following the demolition of the existing conservatory, replacement of the existing part flat roof with a hipped roof section following the demolition of the existing rear dormer, creation of new windows, door openings, and rooflights, and replacement of existing windows and doors. Installation of an enclosed air conditioning unit. Elevational alterations, including the rendering of the existing first floor rear element and the existing render sections. Alterations to the boundary treatment to include new vehicular gates and the formation of a new hard standing to the front of the house.
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.

Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [P8 Rev 1, P10 rev 1, P11 rev 1, P12 rev 1, P13. Received: 17/11/2025. P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P9. Received: 28/10/2025].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 4 - No additional windows or openings shall be formed in the side/rear elevation of the development hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy.

Condition : 5 - The hardstanding hereby permitted shall be made of porous materials, or include provision to direct surface water run-off to a permeable or porous area or surface within the application site, in accordance with the (then) Department for Communities and Local Government publication "Guidance on the permeable surfacing of front gardens" dated September 2008 before the development hereby permitted is first brought into use. The run-off shall not drain into any other foul or surface water drainage system. 
Reason: In order to reduce surface water run-off and the associated pressure on local drainage systems and so prevent flooding.

Condition : 6 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which this permission refers, shall be 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, at all times that the plant operate. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance to the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved. 

b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.   

c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which the application refers, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again.
